commander.web.pair_help: Enter the host's code: 3 digits followed by 3 uppercase letters. Lowercase input is converted automatically. The code expires after 5 minutes. Use only a network you trust.

commander.web.guide_intro: Use the Commander station to share the published tactical picture, record assessments and submit proposals. The local crew remains in control.
commander.web.guide_access_pairing: The host starts the opt-in service and provides a code with three digits followed by three uppercase letters. The code is valid for five minutes. Five failed attempts per rolling minute are allowed across the service. Pairing creates a connection for this browser tab only.
commander.web.guide_access_grant: Pairing permits observations. Annotations and proposals also require the crew to enable the local grant in F9. The grant starts off on every launch and applies only to the current paired connection.
commander.web.guide_access_revoke: The crew can revoke pairing and command permission immediately in F9. Browser Disconnect only forgets this tab's credential; the host pairing remains until its inactivity lease expires or the crew revokes it. A changed world also revokes access.
commander.web.guide_operations_picture: Operations shows the mission summary, published contact register, north-up chart, own-ship status, defensive inventory, damage and bounded event history. Bearing-only observations are rays, never invented positions, and tracks are not extrapolated between snapshots.
commander.web.guide_operations_local: Selecting a contact, panning, zooming, following own ship and editing an unsubmitted form are browser-local actions. They do not select the crew target or send a command.
commander.web.guide_lookout: Lookout is a separate north-up display of the same published observations. Positioned fixes appear as points and bearing-only reports as edge marks. Its range control changes only the browser display; it is not sensor or visual range and does not confirm identity.
commander.web.guide_observations_age: Observation age is time since the latest published measurement. Fix age is time since the latest positioned fix. Older data may remain visible while becoming stale, uncertain or unavailable; a bearing does not supply range.
commander.web.guide_observations_quality: Quality is the current confidence of the published observation, not certainty of identity. Read it with source, age, fix age and bearing or range uncertainty. Missing values stay unavailable rather than being estimated by the browser.
commander.web.guide_observations_annotat: Operator classification and NATO affiliation are manual assessments, not sensor-confirmed truth. They are sent only after Apply, require the local grant and may be rejected if the contact or crew assessment changed.
commander.web.guide_target_proposal: An eligible observed contact can be proposed as a target. The proposal does not assign the crew target, authorize a weapon or fire. The crew must accept or reject it locally.
commander.web.guide_navigation_proposal: A navigation proposal may contain course, speed or both. Blank fields remain unchanged. Acceptance in F9 or the crew message box is mandatory before helm setpoints change, and bridge, engine and quiet-mode limits still apply.
commander.web.guide_message_box: Pending target and navigation proposals open the non-pausing crew message box. Target has priority; F8 switches when both are pending, F6 accepts, F7 rejects, and Escape hides the current notice without deciding it. Pending proposals remain available in F9.
commander.web.guide_reconciliation: HTTP queue acknowledgement is not success. The browser waits for the authoritative crew result and locks further actions. If delivery is uncertain, it never resends automatically; Check / resend uses the identical request and ID, no more than once every five seconds, and may apply it for the first time.
commander.web.guide_eloka_esm: The crew's ELOKA station passively retains up to 64 ESM radar intercepts with bearing, uncertainty, observed frequency, PRF, modulation, quality and age. ESM remains active when own radar is off. Commander Operations does not publish a separate ESM register.
commander.web.guide_eloka_correlation: Emitter candidates use measured signal properties. Radar and sonar correlation uses compatible time, bearing and observed position, never a hidden entity ID. A manually assigned radar type is an operator annotation. Destroyed operations equipment disables ELOKA measurement and control.
commander.web.guide_emcon: The crew controls surface-search and air-search radar emissions separately. Switching a radar off removes that active sensor's new measurements but does not switch off passive ESM. Emitting can make own forces detectable, so the crew must balance radar coverage against EMCON exposure.
commander.web.guide_analyzer_contacts: Contacts is a read-only browser for the packaged unit catalog. Filter profiles and inspect reference dimensions, machinery, systems and generated acoustic analysis diagrams.
commander.web.guide_analyzer_limits: Analyzer selection is independent from the observed contact selected in Operations. A catalog profile is not a live observation, classification, crew target or proposal, and browsing it sends no command.
commander.web.guide_security: Use Commander only on a trusted local network. The host explicitly selects a loopback or private IPv4 address. HTTP traffic is unencrypted and the service is not for Internet exposure. The bearer authorization stays in this tab's memory and is never stored. Reloading or Disconnect forgets it locally; immediate re-pairing may require the crew to revoke the old host pairing in F9.
commander.web.guide_reconnect: The browser retries interrupted snapshot delivery automatically with a bounded delay. While stale, the picture is frozen and all actions are locked; no motion is predicted and old alarm sounds are not replayed. Expired authorization returns to pairing.
commander.web.guide_authority_forbidden: Commander cannot directly steer, fire weapons, operate sensors, change rules of engagement, change time or time acceleration, save or load, or operate mission and unit editors.
commander.web.guide_authority_summary: Remote authority is limited to explicitly applied contact annotations and target or navigation proposals while paired, locally granted and live. Every consequential decision remains with the local crew.

help.note.bridge_noise: Speed means noise: high speed degrades passive sonar and reveals the frigate. Cavitation starts at 15 kn.
help.note.bridge_coast: Coasts: the frigate cannot sail onto land (it is pushed back).
help.note.bridge_tactic: Stopped/4 kn gives the best listening. Sprint in, then go quiet and prosecute tactically.
help.note.passive: Passive sonar provides bearing only (with array- and own-speed-dependent bearing error).
help.note.tma: TMA estimates target position and speed from maneuvers and a bearing series (confidence rises); it does not estimate depth.
help.note.waterfall: Waterfall: newest at top, oldest at bottom. Broadband X is bearing; LOFAR X is frequency. Brightness is relative received level.
help.note.audio_model: Audio and spectra come from the same synthetic listening beam. Multiple sources and own-ship noise may overlap.
help.note.demon: DEMON shows measured modulation, not certain blade rate or identity. FFT windows span up to 2 s; listen for at least 1 s after changing bearing.
help.note.gain: Gain affects display and audio, not detection. D applies band/notch filtering to audio; DEMON analyzes the unfiltered listening beam.
help.note.snr: SNR is based on signal/noise from range, thermocline, sea state, own noise, and towed-array depth.
help.note.shadow: A target below the thermocline is in a shadow zone (lower SNR).
help.note.parallel: HMS and TAS operate in parallel; matching bearings corroborate tracks.
help.note.ghost: A large discrepancy between arrays marks a possible ghost contact.
help.note.tas_handling: TAS performance is available only after complete deployment and stabilization. Deployment/retrieval pauses outside 3-12 kn; overspeed may damage TAS.
help.note.tas_depth: Put TAS below the measured thermocline to hear deep targets.
help.note.active: ACTIVE shows stored echo measurements only: age/fading, bearing, range, and measurement uncertainty.
help.note.sonar_tactic: Listen passively first (at low speed), then ping deliberately. A ping is both a weapon and a warning to the submarine operator.
help.note.roe: ROE STD: the target must be located (ping/TMA) and classified as submarine. ROE FREE requires classification only.
help.note.target_depth: Target depth comes from active ping, not TMA; the wrong depth causes a miss.
help.note.salvo: Salvo doctrine permits at most 2 wire-guided torpedoes in the water.
help.note.weapon_tactic: Obtain depth by ping, then fire. Decoys imitate signatures and may make a contact lose its own frequencies.
help.note.destroyed: DESTROYED means the station is permanently lost.
help.note.sinking: The frigate sinks at 60% average flooding across all compartments.
help.note.fire: Fire spreads; firefighting teams reduce it.
help.note.assignment: Teams can be assigned only to repairable damage; an occupied compartment does not displace another team.
help.note.damage_tactic: Prioritize machinery and sonar, then the hull. Assign a team to fire immediately.
help.note.radar: Radar sees surface vessels and ASMs; submerged submarines remain invisible.
help.note.ais_esm: AIS supplies civilian tracks; passive ESM analysis is available at Electronic Warfare.
help.note.nato: NATO frames: friendly blue, neutral green, hostile red, unknown yellow.
help.note.ciws: CIWS intercepts automatically inside 1.5 NM (limited ammunition).
help.note.jammer: Jammer ASMs beyond 20 NM provide only a HOJ bearing.
help.note.clutter: Radar clutter and measurement interference begin at sea state 5.
help.note.chaff: Chaff makes a missile break lock (40%) or blinds it briefly.
help.note.air_defense: Use chaff and maneuver first, then engage with ESSM. VLS cells are scarce.
help.note.hfdf: HFDF gives bearings (+/-8 degrees) to transmitting submarines (snorkel, HF).
help.note.teletype: Teletype carries HQ bulletins, weather, and ROE changes.
help.note.hfdf_map: Logged bearing lines and cross-fixes appear on the chart.
help.note.hfdf_tactic: Combine an HFDF bearing with a sonar bearing for a position cross-fix.
help.note.cavitation: Above 15 kn, cavitation sharply raises noise and degrades passive sonar.
help.note.engine_damage: Damaged machinery caps speed at 15 kn; destroyed machinery caps it at 8 kn.
help.note.noise_range: Noise percentage indicates own detection/revelation range.
help.note.quiet: QUIET reduces own noise but limits speed to 12 kn.
help.note.engine_tactic: Sprint in (FULL/FLANK), then use SLOW to listen.
help.note.helo_stores: HSP-5 has finite buoy and torpedo stores; launches do not replenish them.
help.note.helo_fuel: Running out of fuel before landing loses HSP-5.
help.note.buoys: Buoys provide passive data and remain active until their batteries expire.
help.note.helo_roe: The target must be classified as submarine before an air-torpedo attack.
help.note.shared_controls: H/B/D are also available at the weapons station. Dipping sonar is not implemented.
help.note.helo_tactic: Lay a buoy field ahead of the suspected target position, then recall HSP-5 in time.
help.note.eloka_passive: ESM remains passive and operates independently of own radar emission.
help.note.eloka_candidates: Candidate radar types are ranked only from observed frequency, PRF, and modulation; ties are not identification.
help.note.eloka_correlation: Radar/sonar links use compatible time, bearing, and observed position, never hidden identity.
help.note.eloka_damage: A destroyed operations center disables ESM; ELOKA shares the existing operations compartment.
help.note.eloka_tactic: Compare candidate fingerprints and independent tracks before entering an operator assignment.
